ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all anticipated directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, the United Kingdom Consolidated List, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the domestic targeted financial sanctions list maintained under South African law. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001, and must follow FIC Guidance Notes 4A and 4B. Positive matches require enhanced risk mitigation, rejection, or cautious approval by the compliance officer, and suspicious transaction reporting is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eServices portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name may be in any of the 11 official South African languages or in English; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for CIPC registration. The name must not be deceptive, offensive, falsely imply state patronage, or conflict with registered names and trademarks. The mandatory suffix for a private limited company is '(Pty) Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the CIPC within 20 business days of receiving the rejection notice, accompanied by the name search receipt and a statement addressing the stated ground for refusal. If the CIPC maintains the refusal, the applicant may escalate the dispute to the Companies Tribunal under section 12 of the Companies Act, 2008, and thereafter seek judicial review in the High Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only for service-of-process and registered-office purposes, provided a physical South African street address is held by the company. However, because the underlying business is a contract pharmaceutical laboratory engaged in peptide synthesis, the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) requires a separate physical manufacturing and laboratory premises, and virtual office arrangements are not acceptable as the principal place of business for regulatory licensing or GMP compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; estimated 70-85% cumulative annual probability of a scheduled or unannounced physical inspection by SAHPRA once pharmaceutical manufacturing authorisation is applied for or granted, with a substantially lower residual risk of CIPC premises inspection for registered-office compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13-19 and 66, read with the Companies Regulations, 2011 (GN R351)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company; shares may be authorized with no par value and issued for the consideration fixed by the board; no escrow deposit requirement applies

II. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search and file Form CoR 9.1 (Reservation of Name) through the CIPC e-Services portal, or elect to incorporate under the temporary registration number. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee via CIPC's secure payment gateway and retain the payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of ID/passport of each incorporator/director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an objection under regulation 14 of the Companies Regulations, 2011 within 20 business days, or resubmit a revised name application reflecting a new distinguishing element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of MOI and Filing of Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal / CIPC Registration Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and execute Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), certifying compliance with s 13(1). Attach the executed MOI and director consents, then submit electronically via CIPC e-Services and pay the statutory registration fee.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1A / CoR 14.2 consent to act as director or auditor
Certified ID copies of directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC may issue a query letter; correct the flagged particulars, amend the MOI where necessary, and resubmit within the prescribed response period. If registration is refused, apply for rectification under s 14(4) with supporting founding documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Share Certificates and Opening of Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / South African banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, pass the share allotment resolution, and issue share certificates. Open a corporate bank account in the company name, providing the bank with the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, board resolution on authorized signatories, and beneficial ownership declaration.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership (BOR) declaration and ID copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries documentation, furnish a supplementary board resolution or amended MOI extracts; for account refusals, approach a second licensed bank or the Banking Ombudsman for guidance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax, VAT and PAYE Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a taxpayer with SARS through eFiling for income tax, and simultaneously apply for VAT if annual taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1 million, and for PAYE/UIF as employer. Submit the required declarations and proof of banking details.
required_dossiers: MOI and proof of residential/business address
Banking confirmation letter and director ID copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS may issue a verification request; provide the requested source documents within 21 business days or apply for a date extension via the SARS branch relationship manager. Overdue registrations are cured by filing the returns and penalty mitigation request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) through the DEL's online system, and obtain a Letter of Good Standing under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) before employing staff.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate and SARS employer number
Proof of business address and bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UIF/COIDA application is disputed, lodge corrected employer schedules with the DEL commissioner and provide proof of prior registrations to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: B-BBEE Affidavit Filing for Exempt Micro Enterprise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If annual turnover is below the EME threshold (ZAR 10 million), complete a sworn B-BBEE affidavit before a Commissioner of Oaths and register the affidavit on the B-BBEE Commission portal. This does not form part of the CIPC incorporation but supports procurement readiness.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For affidavit rejection, correct the declared black ownership percentages and re-file with a newly commissioned affidavit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment Report under Listing Notice 1 (NEMA EIA Regulations, 2014, GN R983) for pharmaceutical laboratory facilities; a full Scoping and EIA (Listing Notice 2, GN R984) applies if chemical storage capacity, solvent volumes, or wastewater discharges exceed listed activity thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge permit under the National Water Act 36 of 1998 (s 21 water use licence) with limits of pH 5.5-9.5, COD <= 75 mg/L, TSS <= 25 mg/L per municipal by-laws; hazardous waste manifesting under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008; VOC and fume emissions controlled under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 (AELs if listed activity triggered; SANS 10400 compliance otherwise)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); online portal: SARS eFiling (www.sars.gov.za / secure.efiling.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity conducting a business in South Africa or having a place of effective management within South Africa must first obtain an income tax reference number from SARS. This requires submission of the CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) registration certificate, memorandum of incorporation, list of directors and the appointed public officer, and proof of registered office and bank account details. The application is lodged through SARS eFiling after creating an eFiling profile. Following income tax registration, VAT registration is applied for using the VAT101 form (with accompanying supporting documents) either online or at a SARS branch, with the SARS vendor reference number (VAT number) issued once the entity meets the turnover threshold or alternatively applies voluntarily. For a non-resident supplier of imported or electronic services, SARS may register the supplier for VAT under the separate non-resident supplier regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a South African (Pty) Ltd is a separate legal taxpayer subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income at 27% (year of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023), with dividends subject to dividends withholding tax at shareholding level and no US-style pass-through status recognised.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under South African law. Statutory elections available include: (i) the participation exemption election in respect of foreign dividends and controlled foreign company (CFC) income under section 9D; (ii) headquarter company elections under sections 9I; (iii) certified emission reduction and innovation allowance elections under the Income Tax Act; (iv) hybrid mismatch rule elections under sections 23M to 23R (including designated instruments); and (v) VAT grouping election under section 50 of the VAT Act. Corporate restructuring roll-over relief, assessed-loss ring-fencing elections, and micro-business turnover elections are also available in specific circumstances.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies (actually received or invoiced) during a 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted from ZAR 50,000. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services (including digitised goods and services) are subject to a separate compulsory registration threshold of ZAR 50,000 in respect of supplies to South African recipients.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not presently mandate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. SARS eFiling is the return submission portal, and SARS eInvoicing is an optional, standards-based electronic tax invoice exchange platform (Tax Invoice e-Invoice) designed to support automated reconciliation; it is not a clearance regime. Taxpayers must maintain complete, accurate records and ensure tax invoices contain all prescribed particulars under the VAT Act. Electronic tax invoices must retain their integrity, legibility, authentic origin, and be available for audit on demand; cryptography or equivalent controls are necessary if the integrity of the information cannot otherwise be demonstrated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies where the supplier is a resident VAT vendor and the goods are physically exported from South Africa to a non-resident within the prescribed timeframes under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, or where services are supplied to a non-resident and performed outside South Africa, are physically supplied outside South Africa, or are directly connected to exported movable property, or constitute international transport services. The economic substance of the export must be evidenced by actual movement of goods or performance of services outside the Republic and payment in foreign currency. The zero-rating claim must be supported with retained documentary proof that the goods left South Africa and that the consideration was received in an amount in foreign currency within 180 days of the date of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) as required under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or road manifest proving physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-issued statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Copy of the agreement or contract with the non-resident customer
Certified evidence of payment and currency conversion, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS conducts substantial audit scrutiny of export zero-rated claims. If export documentation is incomplete, fraudulent, or the foreign currency proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, SARS may reinstate the supply as standard-rated, issue an additional VAT assessment, and impose understatement penalties under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011. Understatement penalties for a substantial (less than 15%) or repeat understatement can reach up to 200% of the tax shortfall in the most serious case, plus interest on the outstanding amount. Intentional false statements and fraudulently obtained refunds expose the taxpayer to criminal prosecution, administrative monetary penalties, and potential VAT vendor deregistration, all without prejudice to exchange-control penalties for non-repatriation of export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), the authorised Exchange Control Administrator under the Currency and Exchanges Act, No. 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is freely convertible on the current account for trade in goods and services, with no rationing or administrative quota. Non-resident capital account transfers are liberalised under SARB policy: inward direct foreign investment requires only a declaration through an Authorised Dealer and a SARS tax compliance certificate at the point of repatriation. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders may be made freely once a dividend is validly declared, provided the company has obtained a SARS dividend tax clearance, has filed any withholding tax obligations (20% final dividend tax, subject to treaty relief), and presents the underlying audited financial statements to the Authorised Dealer. There is no exchange control approval required merely for the payment of genuine dividends out of realised profits, but the disbursement must be effected through the regulated banking system in compliance with the Currencies and Exchanges Act. Proceeds of disposal of a local investment by a non-resident may be remitted back subject to proof that the investment was originally credited through an Authorised Dealer and that all South African taxes (CGT, dividend tax, interest) have been settled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Exchange Control Manual and Circulars, an exporter must repatriate export proceeds of custom synthesised peptides into South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment (date of the Customs Bill of Entry / SAD500). Once credited, the proceeds must be offered for sale to an Authorised Dealer in ZAR within 30 days of receipt unless the exporter maintains a pre-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or a Specialised Foreign Currency Account with the Authorised Dealer, in which case the full 100% may be retained offshore/banking locally for future trade obligations. The de facto mandatory conversion ratio for proceeds received into a domestic ZAR account is 100% (net of any permitted banking fees); the authorised dealer applies the prevailing spot market rate. Exports of peptides require accurate commodity tariff classification and must not be perceived as a transfer of dual-use goods without proper supporting end-user and GMP documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as primary banking rails for a South African company. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or Revolut are not authorised dealers in terms of the SARB exchange-control framework and are generally unable to offer ZAR domestic ACH clearing or to act as a local treasury account holder for compliance with South African exchange control. They may be used as auxiliary payment collection channels for invoices denominated in USD/EUR/GBP, but the funds must be settled through a local Authorised Dealer in order to satisfy the export proceeds repatriation timeline (180 days from shipment / 30 days from credit) and the Verification of Beneficial Ownership requirements under FICA. The bank-grade classification of the CMO laboratory as 'medium-risk enhanced due-diligence' reinforces that an offshore EMI cannot perform the file-and-recall confirmations and foreign currency surrender functions that SARB requires.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for at least one in-country director or local authorised signatory of the (Pty) Ltd for final FATCA/CRS and FICA verification. Where all directors are foreign residents, the bank will normally insist on a face-to-face interview at the branch, a sworn affidavit executed in the presence of a banker, notary public, or South African high commission official, and biometric verification of the individual. A purely remote account opening may be accepted only where the beneficial owners are already known to the financial institution or where a regulated South African compliance officer provides an equivalent assurance; however, for a contract pharmaceutical CMO (ISIC 2100) with a higher-risk profile, physical appearance of the CEO/CFO or of an authorised local compliance officer at the bank branch remains the decisive gate. The bank will also require the presence of an external audit engagement and the production of the Integrated Annual Financial Statements before releasing any unsecured treasury or corporate card facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classification as a manufacturer of therapeutic oligo-peptides raises dual-use or controlled-substance screening alerts, including possible use of peptide chemistry as a precursor for toxic substances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAHPRA (South African Health Products Regulatory Authority) licence for the site-specific peptide synthesis; WHO-GMP certificate for the relevant solid-phase manufacturing building; technical data sheets and the exact CAS registry numbers of the manufactured peptide API; a signed End-User Certificate from every non-resident client; screening reports against the National List of Controlled Substances; verified product origin (custom filing SAD500) and an audit trail of downstream use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injections from foreign PE/VC funds or a parent company in a low-tax / tax-restricted jurisdiction, with no clear beneficial ownership chain, causing source-of-wealth alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date Companies House Equivalent (CIPC) beneficial ownership register filed in terms of the Companies Act; constitutive constitutional documents (MOI, share register); notarised resolutions of the directors approving the issuance of shares; a banking source-of-funds file covering audited financial statements of the foreign parent/fund, tax residency certificates, fund offering memorandum and capital commitment letter, and a confirmation from the SAPR Game/ Public Office-Beard? (Financial Intelligence Centre) that the beneficial owners are not PEPs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual pre-payment / advance payment patterns for peptide API exports through an intermediate trading company, especially if the end-client is undisclosed or counterparty sits in a sanctions-adjacent country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial invoice, signed master service agreement (CMO), the underlying purchase order showing exact peptide sequence and quantity; export declaration (SAD500/EORI) and packing list; freight forwarding airway bill and Bill of Lading; a copy of the syndicated Authorised Dealer's correspondence showing the use of a genuine trade purpose code; a representation letter from the intermediate counterparty identifying the ultimate consignee; and where necessary, a binding legal opinion that the peptides are non-scheduled and non-military-grade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) appearing as non-resident directors or indirectly as beneficial owners of the foreign shareholder; plus the fact that the local company generates Intellectual Property revenue from patented peptide sequences, triggering R&D tax and FX royalty scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening certificates from a reputable third-party database for all directors and 25% beneficial owners; internal source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memoranda; the tax clearance certificate issued by SARS (valid at the time of remittance); a schedule of patents/registered IP transferring into the (Pty) Ltd; board minutes showing the purpose of the capital transaction; and a sworn declaration from the ultimate beneficial owner that their funds originate from lawful employment, investment, or business proceeds, annexed with corroborating bank statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder capital contributions must be transferred by SWIFT wire (or MT103) into a dedicated capital escrow / share subscription account at an SARB Authorised Dealer in South Africa. The remittance instruction must carry the correct SARB Balance of Payments (BOP) purpose code for inward direct investment – generally '7 – Share capital, controlling branch / Disinvestment, as applicable', with the underlying narrative referencing the share allotment resolution and the subscriber's name. The Authorised Dealer requires the multilingual Notarial Fidelity (Form Q1) whichever is no longer mandatory for ordinary share issues, but requires a complete FATCA/CRS questionnaire, a CIPC certificate of incorporation, the resolution of the board issuing shares, and a SARS entity tax-compliance certificate. After receipt, the bank will verify that the wire matches the declared principal, will quarantine for source-of-funds checks (3-5 days), and will then credit the operating account; no further SARB approval is required for a bona fide inbound capital contribution, but the transaction must be recorded on the bank's BOP data system and the share issuance must be filed with CIPC within 30 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearance for outbound trade settlements (payments for raw materials, lab consumables, and external peptide synthesis resins) must be executed through the SARB Authorised Dealer using the standard international payment instruction SWIFT MT103 for direct remittances. The authorised dealer requires the mandatory Form C/CD/IP/CC plus a SARS declaration and the corresponding trade documents: commercial invoice, packing list, carriage contract, and, for letters of credit, an irrevocable documentary credit opened by SWIFT MT700/MT707 with a conforming set of negotiable shipping documents. The company may also utilise an open-account settlement with its foreign suppliers by issuing an MT103 under the 'Goods' purpose code, supported by an import declaration (Form CC or the electronic duty approval). For recurring licensing and technical support fees, use the current-account purpose code 'Royalties / license fees' and submit the IP licence agreement, SARS tax clearance, and a transfer-pricing bench total (OECD ALP) memo. Any payment to a non-resident from ZAR funds requires the bank to verify that the local liquidity is not contaminated by unrepatriated export proceeds; therefore the bank may require an 'Export Payment Allocation Certificate' if a specific export is being offset.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward: permitted for hedge of commercial exposures (USD/EUR/GBP vs ZAR) for up to 12 months, with no speculative build-up and monthly confirmation to the FX advisor.

Non-deliverable forward matched to future orders/zero-deliverable net settlement: allowed where the counterparty is an authorised dealer and the underlying production order is demonstrable on approved trade documentation.
Cross-currency interest-rate swap: permitted for risk management of foreign currency debt or capital leasing; requires recorded underlying liability and evidence of the financing arrangement.

FX option / collar structures (costless collar, zero-cost participation) for protection against extraordinary rand weakness, requiring an Analytical risk certificate and no naked premium selling without sufficient liquid collateral.

Currency swap with a non-resident parent for optimal netting of intercompany liquidity: permissible only under SARB Exchange Control approval where the notional amount is within the foreign credit exposure limits and supported by a full transfer-pricing and treasury-policy document.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CoR 44.1) — CIPC annual good-standing filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Republic of South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date. CIPC fee bands are turnover-based: R100 (approx USD 6) for turnover below R1 million; R150 (approx USD 8) for R1m–R10m.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a CIPC penalty equal to the prescribed annual-return fee, a compliance notice, and suspension of good-standing certificates. Failure to file for two consecutive years, or to pay prescribed fees for two consecutive years, permits CIPC to strike the company off the register under s.82(4) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 after notice, with company property vesting in the State as bona vacantia pending restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Return — annual confirmation and event-driven update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register portal (Companies Act s.56, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be lodged within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; a share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership or control must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-filing is a continuing offence under the Companies Act; directors may be personally fined, CIPC may issue compliance notices, the Annual Return filing is blocked, and the company is flagged non-compliant for bank and counterparty due diligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) — preparation, board approval and shareholder presentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders; filed with CIPC where the company is public or state-owned or a filing duty is imposed by regulation or the MOI; retained for SARS audit purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepare, approve and sign the AFS within 6 months after the financial year-end (common private-company year-end: 28/29 February); present to shareholders at a general meeting within the same period where the MOI requires an AGM.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors in breach of s.30/31 may receive compliance notices, financial penalties and personal liability declarations; where a mandatory audit is omitted, the AFS are non-compliant, the Annual Return is rejected, and directors may face disqualification proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ITR14 Corporate Income Tax Return (with taxable income reconciliation and AFS attachments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (for a 28/29 February year-end: by end-February of the following tax season); provisional tax payments fall due at the mid-year and year-end points of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic administrative non-compliance penalty under s.210–211 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: percentage-of-assessed-tax penalty escalating monthly (from approximately 10% in month one, capped at 20%), plus interest at the prescribed rate; continued default can lead to criminal prosecution of directors and SARS enforcement actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full statutory audit is mandatory where the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 500 or more; for all public companies and state-owned companies; or where the MOI or a regulator (e.g., pharmaceutical licensing authority for a licensed CDMO) requires it. PIS is scored annually per s.26 of the Companies Act (points for employees, third-party liabilities, turnover, shareholding spread, and subsidiary holdings). Private companies with PIS below 500 may instead obtain an independent review; owner-controlled companies with PIS below 350 may be exempt from both audit and review and use compilation-only statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (full) is required for public, state-owned and large private companies; private companies may apply IFRS for SMEs (SA); non-profit companies must use a CIPC-approved framework. All AFS must satisfy the fair-presentation test in s.29, be approved and signed by a director per s.32, and be retained with the company's records.
